title: Families Pack United High School for UISD's 2026 Parent Learning Summit
excerpt: Parents from across United ISD packed United High School for the district's 2026 Parent Learning Summit, a day of sessions on college readiness, special education, health and more — an event the district has run for nearly 20 years.
content:
Parents from across United Independent School District packed United High School for the district’s 2026 Parent Learning Summit, turning the annual event into a full day of sessions, one-on-one conversations and family activities.

The summit, which the district has held for nearly 20 years, is designed to connect families with the district’s programs, resources and opportunities. This year’s sessions covered college readiness, health and nutrition, fine arts, special education, Section 504 services and parent engagement, among others, and campus teams were on hand to talk with parents one-on-one about resources tailored to their children’s needs.

Superintendent Dr. Gerardo Cruz said student success depends on the partnership between schools and families, calling that collaboration essential to maintaining the district’s A-rated standard.

Keynote speaker Josh Perez of 360 Athletics encouraged families to take an active role in planning for their children’s future, and presenter Patricia Valenzuela led a session on parents’ emotional and mental well-being, urging caregivers to look after their own health while supporting their children.

Board President Michelle Molina, speaking as a parent of a child with special needs, said the summit gives families a chance to learn what the district offers and what their rights are. Trautmann parent Daniel Villarreal, attending for the first time, called it an outstanding event and recommended it to parents who have never gone, while Maribel and Manuel Lee of Clark Middle School attended with their two children to learn about workshops and extracurricular activities.

Local community agencies joined district departments at the event, giving parents a single place to find support services, including some many did not know were available. The summit was coordinated by the district’s Federal and State Programs Department, led by Director Sara Hernandez, who called parent engagement the cornerstone of student success.

Although the summit has wrapped up, the resources shared there remain available year-round through campus counselors, principals and the Federal and State Programs Department.

Sources: United Independent School District — “Families Pack United High School for UISD’s 2026 Parent Learning Summit,” Nov. 20, 2026, https://www.uisd.net/159333_2?articleID=86566
